title: Algorithms
overview: A focused revision guide to algorithms.

sections.title: Searching
content: Linear search: checks every item, works unsorted, O(n). Binary search: halves the search space each time, needs sorted data, O(log n).

sections.title: Sorting
content: Bubble sort: swaps adjacent out-of-order pairs repeatedly, O(n²). Insertion sort: builds a sorted section by inserting each item into place. Be ready to trace either step-by-step.

examTips: When comparing algorithms, state both the Big O and a practical reason — e.g. "binary search is O(log n) so it scales far better than linear search's O(n)".
